prompt: The Leaning Tower of Pisa. TWO CRITICAL FEATURES: (1) it must clearly LEAN - tilt the whole tower so the top is offset 5-6 blocks sideways from the base, an obvious dramatic lean. (2) It must show 8 STACKED TIERS of open arched colonnades - each tier is a ring of evenly-spaced STONE/SNOW columns with AIR gaps between them (open arcade galleries you can see through), then a solid floor ring, then the next tier up. This stacked-arcade look is the tower's identity - do NOT make a plain smooth or lumpy cylinder. A round tower about 7 blocks in diameter and 30 tall, 8 visible tiers, the bottom tier a solid base, the top a slightly narrower bell chamber. White marble palette: SNOW and STONE only, a little COBBLE trim. Stand it on a GRASS lawn. Composition: tall round tower dead-center facing the viewer (-Z), leaning obviously to one side, the stacked tiers and column arches clearly visible against the sky. Iconic, elegant, tilted. Use the full solid-block budget on a tiered, arcaded, LEANING tower.
